verdict: Area's foundations are strong and rare, and the render confirms them: the cap-based inset contract (Button, Chip, Segmented, Menu, Checkbox and Radio measure a cap offset of 0.00 on every tile), concentric corners stated as a rule, inks solved per ground under every setting, ordered state fills, top-layer overlays on the platform and motion as tokens end to end. None of the fifteen design systems or six live products derives padding, corners and inks this way.

The weakness is uniformity, not taste. Six root causes: (1) the defaults moved (type 14 → 13, corner 8 → 10) and formulas, comments and families written for the old defaults were not carried, so values land between rungs (gap-row 10, radius-step 10 against an 8 medium control, a 17 line, an 11 corner); (2) families built in different sessions restate the same part (frame, row, field shell, header bar, mark, popup surface) with small differences, so seven card corners and four mark heights render side by side; (3) behaviour is written per family (five menu engines, five typeaheads, three roving models) and tested in none; (4) against shipped products Area is about twice as slow in overlay motion, roomier and rounder in floating lists, heavier in dark washes, one text ink short and compressed in dark (muted 1.49:1 from default); (5) hierarchy is flat (nothing above 20/28 and 500); (6) nothing rendered is tested, so drift returns, and the gallery's own defects (tile names, bleeding stages, demos that hide their state) make good components look unfinished.

Done looks like this: one recipe per shared part read by every family, a rendered check per rule that fails when a value drifts, the references' range reached where the owner chooses it (motion, menu density, corners, washes, inks), the other worktree's heading tokens adopted, and every family scoring at least 4 on balance, spacing, type, shape, colour and feel in the same capture.

One manifest, a parity check and an orthogonal registry are rare (B §5); but six listbox implementations with no shared keyboard hook (B-S4), no frame part (BL-C2) and a slot vocabulary in five spellings (B-S1).
Cap centring exact in Button, Menu, Checkbox (VA §2); off by 0.6 in a dozen families (VN8, VA1), Switch 3 px high in Setting row (VA3), Panel on two grids (VN16), templates 79 px empty (VC20).
Card-like frames use seven corners (VC3), marks four heights and three corners (VS2), eight header bars (G6, VN7), five open-trigger paints (S3).

Toasts render inert under modals (I3); required pickers submit empty (I6); 11 families have targets under 24 with no hit expansion (G3).
Tooltip hardening and Combobox match or beat the libraries (RB §8); submenus close on the way to them (I1, RB1), five menu engines (I2), overlays about twice the references' duration (RC3).
Motion is tokens end to end and every hover is media-gated (I §5, S §4); literal fills (S6, S20), stale default numbers in ~25 comments (G19, T25, S17), CSS files not named by family (B-S15).
Two text inks where references use three (RC8, RF1); dark muted only 1.49:1 from default (RL1); hierarchy stops at 20/28 500 (T16, RL4).

63 settings with solved inks per ground, ordered state fills and scoped re-derivation, which no reference has (RD §2.10); no typeface setting (RD16), brand second and third colours read by nothing (B-S16).
A 3.4 MB unminified stylesheet in one entry (I18); no memo or windowing anywhere (I17); synchronous layout work on every scroll in every menu (I9).
No shipped compositions, every recreation rebuilt the shell (B-P1); no responsive or safe-area rules (B-P2); mobile, media and calendar the weakest product types (B §4.1).
